scenario: Two headless turns sharing one session. Turn 1 (fresh) sends 'reply ALPHA' and the model streams ALPHA. Turn 2 re-launches the SAME binary with `--resume <session_id>` and sends 'reply BETA'. Question: does the resumed process re-emit turn 1's assistant content (ALPHA) on stdout? Determines whether parse_assistant.go's never-streamed snapshot recovery duplicates history on every reopen/crash-recovery.
finding: case_A — resume does NOT re-emit historical assistant content on stdout

key_observations.turn2_only_isReplay_envelope: the just-sent user message (BETA), echoed by --replay-user-messages with isReplay:true; NO assistant envelope carried isReplay
key_observations.interpretation: Turn 2's envelope counts are IDENTICAL to turn 1's (one assistant, one user). A resume that replayed history would show extra assistant/user envelopes for turn 1's content. It shows none — `--resume` loads prior turns into the model's context silently and streams only the NEW turn.

reconciliation: Spike-verified here: ASSISTANT text/thinking is NOT re-emitted on resume, and the only isReplay:true envelope is the just-sent user message. NOT tested here: whether historical user-role tool_results re-fire on resume — design notes elsewhere claim --resume 'replays the full session log including tool_results'; that would be a separate user-path mechanism (parse_user_replay.go), not the assistant path. Either way it is irrelevant to the snapshot-recovery path in parse_assistant.go, which only touches `assistant` envelopes.
purpose: Backs the safety argument for the streamedMessageIDs discriminator (parser.go) and the never-streamed snapshot recovery (parse_assistant.go): a bare `assistant` snapshot with no in-process message_start is always an in-turn CLI-internal retry, never replayed history. Recovery therefore cannot duplicate the assistant history on reopen. See claude-wire.md §'Resume does not re-emit assistant content'.
